title: The Keelboat Voyage to Rehevä
dek: A grateful father funds a keelboat, five companions learn to sail under pressure, and repairs and strangers’ hospitality carry them to the cliff-top community of Rehevä.

facts.People: Loistava; Dale; Olokun; Lucido Spettoro; Alyhotep bin Baladin; Targas Tarmile; Mogh
facts.Outcome: All five reach Rehevä; later exploration and proposed improvements remain ahead

body:
The boat waiting at Eovar was rented, cramped and crewless. Targas Tarmile had paid for it because his daughter had come home alive from an earlier rescue. Loistava, Dale, Olokun, Lucido and Alyhotep would have to turn that gift into a voyage themselves.

Beyond the harbor lay violent currents, sharks and a destination known mostly by rumor. The company reached it by surviving the crossing, accepting help and doing the hard work that remained after each danger passed.

A rescue pays for a passage

Targas Tarmile met them at Eovar Harbor with a rented keelboat. It was barely large enough for the company, but it was what he could afford. His daughter Rina had been among the women rescued from an underground trafficking operation. He had learned these travelers were companions of the rescuers and wanted to help their next journey. Dale recognized Saray’s part in bringing her home.

The boat came with a map, a few boards, two hammers and nails for trouble. It did not come with a crew. The local hands were afraid of the route. Targas advised the more agile travelers to steer and the stronger ones to row; he warned them about the current around the bend and the sharks beyond it. Most people he knew had not traveled farther.

Lucido’s familiarity with ports sounded reassuring until he admitted that it came largely from listening to sailors in taverns. He had never put out to sea himself. Loistava had never rowed. Olokun looked at the company anew, then accepted that they would have to manage together. Alyhotep arrived on his floating tablet just before departure, to affectionate greetings and complaints that they had nearly left without him.

They tied ropes around themselves and balanced their places in the boat. Dale thought Olokun was leading. Olokun answered that they were a unit and he would speak when his knowledge could help. Their voyage began with borrowed means, uneven experience and a willingness to learn in public.

Between the cliffs

At first the tide and wind carried them without much rowing. Then the rock walls rose on either side and the current began pushing the keelboat about. Lucido and Alyhotep kept it clear of the cliffs. Dale put his strength into an oar. Loistava used her command of the wind, while Olokun watched the water and the sail.

The bend was worse. Rushing water struck the rocks and tried to carry them forward when they needed to turn. Lucido, busy encouraging Dale, mishandled his own assistance. Loistava stumbled as the boat lurched. Her wind alone could not cancel a current driving in the wrong direction.

Olokun tried to shape the water toward the turn while Loistava worked with the sail. Lucido leaned his weight into the maneuver when his oar seemed useless. Strength, balance and magic all had to serve the same change of course. They passed close to the rocks before finally emerging into quieter water.

The companions congratulated one another. Dale thought they had made it; Loistava called it an adventure. As the sun lowered, Lucido noticed movement swirling under the keelboat. The calm stretch was not empty.

Sharks beneath the boat

Lucido warned the others that something was under them. Darkness was coming on. He lit his shield so they could see, and Dale put on his night goggles. Several companions could make out what looked like sharks. Olokun and Dale hoped remaining in the boat would be enough to avoid a fight.

It was not. The creatures attacked the keelboat itself. Lucido called for the oars to be brought in before they lost their means of movement. Loistava helped awkwardly with equipment she was still learning. Alyhotep hesitated to hurt hungry creatures, but the danger to the boat and his friends forced the question.

Water began wetting their feet. Then it came in faster. Olokun jumped into the sea to fight the sharks before they could do more damage. The others defended the vessel with their own attacks and magic. Their success in ending the threat did not keep the hull afloat by itself.

When the attack was over, the narrator’s verdict was plain: the boat was sinking. Loistava had slowed the flooding, but there was already too much water aboard. The journey’s next test required the repair supplies Targas had thought to provide, and hands that were tired from steering and fighting.

A boat held together for now

Loistava mended the damaged hull while Dale worked with the spare boards. Alyhotep offered help. Lucido used a magical hand to hold the nails steady so the rolling boat would not turn every hammer stroke into an injured thumb. Olokun tried a more unlikely patch, pushing a shark’s body into a hole to stop the flow.

The repairs helped without making the keelboat sound. A small stream still entered as Loistava continued working. Alyhotep saw land close by and offered to ferry people there one at a time on his tablet if the boat could not be saved. Olokun suggested using it to pull the vessel while he pushed from the water. These were alternatives they considered, not a recorded evacuation by tablet.

Night wore on and the company grew tired. Olokun asked whether they should keep going or seek land. Lucido wanted dry ground and worried the blood in the water might attract more sharks. Dale thought a rest on the water too dangerous. Given space, he could offer shelter ashore.

The hull had been mended enough to hold for the moment. Olokun climbed back aboard, and the others took up the oars again. A fire flickered on the land ahead. Reaching it was a decision to stop and recover, not proof that the boat’s damage or the rest of the voyage had ceased to matter.

Mogh’s shore

The people waiting by the fire appeared to be druids. Their concern did not look like aggression. One man invited the travelers to eat and rest, offering roast goat, fresh water and tents. The invitation itself made some of the company cautious: Lucido found it odd that their hosts would leave strangers beside the fire and go to sleep.

Dale and Alyhotep nevertheless read the man as genuine. Dale accepted the food. Loistava preferred her own fruit and water, staying close to Alyhotep. The different responses did not uncover a hidden attack. Mogh’s people gave them food and room to recover while they decided how far to trust the welcome.

Olokun asked about the island farther on. Their host knew it as Rehevä. It was only a few hours across, he said, but reaching the top meant climbing dangerous stairs cut into the cliff or hauling a platform upward by pulley. What had been a rumored destination at Eovar was a place this man could name and describe.

He introduced himself as Mogh before turning in. He had supplied directions and room to recover without demanding a bargain. The company still chose to sleep together in Dale’s shelter rather than divide among the offered tents.

Cards, sleep and another departure

Dale shuffled a deck and let its cards assemble into a house. He had been eager for the chance to use it, a fact Olokun recognized immediately. There was room for the company and a door he could lock. After the leaking keelboat and the long struggle with the oars, his pleasure in providing a comfortable place was easy to share.

Lucido and Alyhotep offered to watch; Olokun offered the next turn. The company went inside. The night passed without an incident. In the morning Olokun praised the house’s comfort, and Dale returned it to a deck with a tap. That uneventful rest belongs to the journey as much as the attacks: the strangers ashore had not become an ambush simply because some of the travelers feared one.

Mogh pointed toward distant clouds and advised an early departure if they wanted to reach Rehevä before the storm. Loistava wondered whether to wait. Dale wanted to return the hospitality. Mogh told them they owed him nothing and should follow the path their hearts led them toward.

Their hosts’ kindness also provoked a smaller argument before they left. Dale wondered how concern for living things fitted with the goat they had eaten; Lucido offered possibilities rather than a confirmed doctrine. Then the companions said their farewells and set off. Calm water and a favorable breeze carried them toward the towering island.

The platform above the sea

A few hours later, Rehevä’s cliff rose over the boat. The travelers found Mogh’s two approaches: the precarious stairs and the platform hauled by its own pulley. Dale offered his strength. Alyhotep could fly others upward one at a time, but Olokun wanted the company to arrive together in case trouble waited above.

They chose the platform for those who needed it, while the fliers stayed close. Loistava used the wind to ascend. Alyhotep flew with her and sent Wraps ahead. The owl saw a thriving community among greenery and adobe-style buildings. Alyhotep reported the view to the others. The greenery and buildings belonged to a community already living above the cliffs.

Dale and Olokun took the rope. Lucido admitted he had little strength but went with the group. Arms tired and sweat ran down their faces as the platform rose. At last they reached the top and looked out in wonder. Rehevä had entered the company’s traveled world.

Lucido was already thinking about meeting the inhabitants and what Pristinia might offer them. Olokun had suggested improving the difficult access. Those were openings for later work, not completed trade arrangements or a rebuilt harbor. The recovered expedition ends at the arrival, before a full exploration of the community.

Mogh already knew Rehevä’s name and approaches; the people above its cliffs had a history the arrivals still had to learn. After the leaking boat, the night ashore and the last pull on the rope, the five companions were ready to meet them.
